papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing; isoflurane recovery produced transient rebound arousal, fragmented NREM, and persistent ultra-slow oscillations normalizing within two weeks, with cortical transcriptomics distinct from sleep deprivation (integrated stress response/unfolded protein response enrichment vs. growth-permissive mTOR-associated profile).

papers.title: Multi-parametric spectral modeling disentangles synaptic kinetics and neural excitability from non-invasive electrophysiological recordings
papers.summary: Introduces a biologically informed multi-parametric spectral analysis of electrophysiological recordings that disentangles neural excitability from synaptic kinetics, and demonstrates in a proof-of-concept that it captures hyperexcitability and glutamate reuptake dysfunction signatures characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
papers.summary: Proposed SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework using cross-domain alignment for domain-generalizable sleep stage classification from raw heterogeneous EEG/EOG, and reported superior performance versus existing approaches across five sleep staging datasets under domain generalization settings.

papers.title: The ovarian cycle and estradiol modulate cortical network state and auditory entrainment in mice and women
papers.summary: Compared cortical network activity at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation across low- and high-estradiol ovarian cycle phases in mice and women (with EEG and intracortical LFP), finding that high endogenous or exogenous estradiol steepened the aperiodic spectral slope and attenuated auditory entrainment, while increasing fast-spiking interneuron 40-Hz firing but reducing its temporal coherence.

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.summary: This study introduces concept bottleneck models for EEG pathology detection that use analytically computed clinical EEG biomarkers (e.g., band power, spectral ratios, phase locking values) as an interpretable bottleneck. The models approach black-box baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but show lower performance on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%), with a pure CBM variant exhibiting concept fidelity concerns mitigated by increasing concept loss weight.

papers.title: Single-Lead EEG-based virtual reality motion sickness detection using interpretable feature selection.
papers.summary: Proposes a SHAP-based single-lead EEG modeling and feature-screening framework for lightweight virtual reality motion sickness detection, selecting lead FT11 and seven handcrafted features for XGBoost classification. Under window-level tenfold cross-validation it achieved 87.53% ± 0.73% accuracy, with a post hoc LOSO test showing limited cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.summary: Characterized seizure susceptibility in a fully humanized Atn1Q112/+ DRPLA mouse model and tested an antisense oligonucleotide targeting CAG-expanded ATN1. Saline-treated mutants showed increased seizure propensity and early death, while ASO treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, prevented spontaneous behavioral seizures, and protected against early death.

papers.title: Artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation reveals phase-specific modulation of the human visual cortex
papers.summary: Develops a front-end analogue low-pass filtering and per-recording artefact verification pipeline to record artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation, then tests phase-specific neuromodulation of the visual cortex in 22 healthy participants. In-phase 15.5 Hz TI increased SSVEP amplitude at 14.5 and 15.5 Hz and shortened response times relative to sham and anti-phase TI.

papers.title: Template-Anchored Signal Decomposition and Label Refinement for Impairment Categorization on Noisy Visual Electrophysiological Data.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Constructs a dataset of ERG and VEP recordings from 1,970 participants and proposes a template-anchored signal decomposition method with joint channel-spatial attention and soft-label refinement for three-class visual impairment categorization. The method consistently outperformed existing electrophysiology-based and general biosignal classification approaches.

papers.title: Alpha-range neural oscillations are associated with multiple dynamic brain networks
papers.summary: Uses two independent resting-state EEG-fMRI datasets (n=94 discovery, n=33 replication) to show that low- and high-alpha (8-12 Hz) periods are associated with multiple dynamic BOLD coactivation patterns rather than a single static network. Low-alpha periods were mainly linked to unique visual, sensorimotor, attention, and posterior thalamic configurations, while default, control, and attention network patterns overlapped across low- and high-alpha periods.

papers.title: Sleep underestimation and subjective sleep appraisal: Limited value of routine polysomnographic and electroencephalographic features.
papers.summary: In a single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study of 225 adults undergoing clinical polysomnography, self-rated sleep quality was more consistently associated with sleep underestimation than routine PSG/EEG features, and none of 600 EEG features survived FDR correction; an EEG-enhanced model added no out-of-fold discrimination beyond a three-predictor baseline (AUC 0.6564 vs. 0.6786).

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study.
papers.summary: Introduces Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (ConvKAN and ConvKAN Efficient) for EEG-based depression classification on frequency-domain features using the EDRA dataset. ConvKAN Efficient achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 94%, outperforming conventional CNN and traditional machine learning methods.

papers.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
papers.summary: Introduced a QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent EEG classification of English- and Turkish-associated signals, achieving 96.37% accuracy with four channels using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The authors note that the results are not definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding due to confounding between language and participant population.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of training in Brain-Computer Interface: A Biophysical modeling approach
papers.summary: Introduced a biophysical linear neural mass model (mi-NMM) of motor imagery BCI fitted to simultaneous MEG/EEG from 19 healthy subjects across four training sessions; task-dependent modulation of scale-free dynamics revealed training-induced excitatory-inhibitory reconfiguration shifting from widespread cortical to targeted sensorimotor recruitment, with excitatory population time constants linked to MI-related desynchronization and synchronization.

papers.title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
papers.summary: Single-pulse TMS-EEG in healthy adults (n=29 M1, n=11 DLPFC) showed a strong negative relationship between the pre-stimulus aperiodic exponent and early local TMS-evoked potential amplitude in both regions, with steeper 1/f-like slopes associated with smaller EL-TEPs and inconsistent alpha/beta power relationships.

papers.title: Should I "stay" or should I "go"? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking.
papers.summary: Mobile EEG and accelerometry in 14 healthy adults showed that anticipating a stop during overground walking increased step-interval variability and reorganized gait-phase cortical dynamics, with attenuated/delayed left frontotemporal theta desynchronization during swing and altered centroparietal alpha/beta synchronization. The authors interpret this as a shift from automated locomotion toward active monitoring via proactive inhibition.

papers.title: Dorsolateral prefrontal TMS-evoked N100 as a neurophysiological correlate of symptom change in adolescent depression.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 54 adolescents with major depressive disorder, TMS-EEG showed that TMS-evoked dorsolateral prefrontal N100 amplitudes decreased from pre- to post-intervention; reductions in right-hemispheric N100 were significantly associated with improved depressive symptoms, particularly in girls. The authors propose the N100 as a candidate neurophysiological correlate of symptom change.

papers.title: Coupled cardio-pulmonary-cerebral functional dynamics for high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: Using porcine cardiac arrest experiments, this study applied cross- and joint recurrence quantification analysis to arterial blood pressure, EEG, and end-tidal CO2 to quantify cardio-pulmonary-cerebral coupling across baseline, cardiac arrest, CPR, and ROSC. Coupling measures distinguished physiological states, and the T7 cortical region was identified as most sensitive to the CPR process.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: In 182 first-episode major depressive disorder patients and 95 healthy controls, resting-state EEG microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in patients with lifetime auditory hallucination experiences than in those without and in controls, and remained independently associated with such experiences (OR = 1.773) after covariate adjustment, though discrimination was modest (AUC = 0.614).

papers.title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
papers.summary: Intracranial stereoelectroencephalography in eight epilepsy patients performing a near-threshold audiovisual detection task revealed a largely supramodal cortical detection code (including insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, superior temporal gyrus) whose multivariate decoders generalized across modalities, and a substantially supramodal confidence architecture including cross-modal confidence coding in sensory cortices.

papers.title: Corollary discharge dysfunction in auditory verbal hallucinations: N100 suppression measured with semi-dry electrodes.
papers.summary: In 14 patients with persistent auditory verbal hallucinations and 15 healthy controls, N100 suppression during self-generated versus played-back sounds was measured with semi-dry EEG electrodes; healthy controls showed a non-significant trend toward greater suppression, and suppression correlated negatively with hallucination severity (r = -0.54, p = 0.047). The authors interpret this as support for impaired corollary discharge as a mechanistic basis for auditory hallucinations, pending larger-sample replication.

papers.title: Retrospective attention strengthens a report-independent neural signature of visual perception
papers.summary: Using masked retrospective cues and a Report/No-report EEG design, this study found that valid retrospective cues improved orientation discrimination and strengthened a late neural representation of the target even without explicit report; a decoder trained on no-report trials predicted visibility and discrimination in report trials. The results indicate retrospective attention acts on a report-independent perceptual representation, with explicit report amplifying the effect.

papers.title: Responses to unannounced rule changes in adults with developmental disabilities: A community-based pilot study with consumer-grade EEG
papers.summary: In a community-based pilot with adults with developmental disabilities, a probabilistic reversal learning task and consumer-grade resting-state EEG showed wide interindividual variation in switch bias; a flatter frontal aperiodic spectrum was associated with fewer switches after negative feedback and more perseverative errors, and frontal alpha peak amplitude correlated with accuracy. The authors present this as preliminary evidence that field EEG can capture individual differences in responses to unannounced change.

papers.title: Passive Hyperthermia Increases Neural Recruitment, Thereby Reducing Processing Efficiency During Executive Task Performance.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: In 18 healthy adults, passive hyperthermia (~1.1°C rise in ear canal temperature) expanded task-related BOLD activation across frontal, parietal, temporal, and subcortical regions while reducing P300 amplitude and reaction times during Go/No-go and Flanker tasks, suggesting reduced processing efficiency and increased neural strain. Cerebral perfusion (internal carotid and vertebral artery flow) was also reduced, so the authors caution that BOLD findings require careful interpretation.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG was compared between 74 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls, analyzing spectral power and functional connectivity across multiple bands. No EEG contrast survived correction for multiple comparisons, indicating that large or widespread alterations were not detectable; occipital/global alpha power and temporal theta showed only nominal differences.

papers.title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial (N=83) compared a brief music-based auditory intervention to pink noise on subjective and psychophysiological anxiety measures. Cortisol and midline theta power showed significant Condition × Time interactions, but these were not retained in models with all physiologically valid observations, and self-reported anxiety decreased across both conditions.

papers.title: Selection vs. integration task demands shape the similarity of information neural coding
papers.summary: Using EEG in a cue-target size-judgment paradigm, the study examined how selection versus integration task demands shape neural coding during preparation and target processing. Decoding showed categorical templates active in both phases under selection but only during preparation under integration, and RSA indicated exemplar encoding sustained post-stimulus during selection but not integration.

papers.title: Cooperative processing of visual threat across collicular pathways
papers.summary: Combining cell-type-specific inhibition, large-scale electrophysiology, and functional ultrasound imaging, the study shows that inhibiting either narrow-field or wide-field superior colliculus neurons impairs escape to overhead visual threats, so both parallel pathways contribute. Deeper-layer superior colliculus activity selectively represented escape-associated stimuli and predicted escape initiation and vigor, supporting a cooperative circuit architecture for visually evoked defensive behavior.

papers.title: Phasic and tonic pain serve distinct functions during adaptive behaviour
papers.summary: In an immersive virtual reality EEG foraging task, brief phasic pain to the grasping hand reduced choice probability while tonic pressure pain to the contralateral arm reduced action velocities. A free-operant computational framework linked tonic and phasic pain to reduced motivational vigour and decision value, respectively, supporting distinct adaptive functions.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Design and Access: Toward Visual Scene Displays for Brain-Computer Interface Use in Augmentative and Alternative Communication by Children.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.summary: In 24 neurotypical children aged 8–13, asymmetric placement of items in photographic visual scene displays increased frontal and centro-parietal P300 amplitudes and contextual scenes enhanced the occipital N170, while offline predicted P300 BCI accuracy was similar to a standard grid and scenes were rated more visually appealing. The findings support preliminary feasibility of integrating contextual scene displays into pediatric BCI augmentative and alternative communication.

papers.title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
papers.summary: This study establishes and validates a reproducible agarose-phantom pipeline for assessing TMS safety with implanted sEEG electrodes across single-pulse, 1–50 Hz repetitive, and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement stayed micrometer-scale (max transient 10.99 μm), temperature increases remained far below the 2°C threshold (max 0.073°C), and induced voltages and charge densities remained within established safety limits, providing a standardized framework for future TMS-sEEG safety testing.

papers.title: Audience Gaze and Felt Social Connection With Individual Performers During Live Dance.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: Eye movements and mobile EEG were recorded from 88 audience members during a 16-hour live dance performance to study engagement and social connection. Gaze toward performers had a significant indirect association with felt social connection via self-reported focus on individual performers, and EEG alpha power decreased while delta/gamma power increased when dance was accompanied by music.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.summary: In an EEG study, participants viewed sequential gratings whose orientation was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated while judging tilt direction of a task-relevant colored grating. Prediction reduced P3b amplitude only for task-relevant stimuli, and predicted task-relevant gratings were decodable by multivariate pattern analysis and elicited faster responses, supporting joint modulation of late perceptual and decision-related processing by action-based prediction and top-down attention.

papers.title: Selective mGlu1 Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model.
papers.summary: Using a subchronic phencyclidine NMDA hypofunction mouse model, mGlu1 positive allosteric modulators, and SST-interneuron-specific mGlu1 deletion, this study showed that mGlu1 activation restored prefrontal inhibitory transmission and reversed working memory and novel object recognition deficits, effects abolished by deleting mGlu1 from somatostatin-expressing GABAergic interneurons.

papers.title: Dorsomedial striatum calcium permeable AMPA receptors in the development of aversion-resistant alcohol drinking.
papers.summary: Using Western blot, microinjection, and ex vivo electrophysiology in C57BL/6J mice, this study found that dorsomedial striatum calcium-permeable AMPA receptors (CP-AMPARs) initially act to prevent aversion-resistant quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking, but after repeated binges drive aversion-resistant drinking and show greater inward rectification and antagonist sensitivity in dorsomedial striatum spiny projection neurons.

papers.title: Mapping the Research Landscape and Global Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Event-related Potential in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Bibliometric analysis of Web of Science publications on event-related potentials in Alzheimer's disease, covering publication trends, collaboration networks, and keyword clustering; identified six research themes (P300/N200, MMN, N170, N400, OERP, EEG) and suggested mismatch negativity as a future hotspot.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a young woman who developed acute psychosis and dissociative syndrome after binge recreational nitrous oxide and MDMA use, with elevated homocysteine indicating functional cobalamin deficiency, normal brain MRI and EEG, and full recovery after vitamin B12 supplementation and antipsychotic treatment (aripiprazole after risperidone-induced neutropenia).

papers.title: Narrow Is Slow: CT-Derived Anatomic Isthmus 3 Width and Arrhythmogenic Substrate in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
papers.summary: In a retrospective single-center study of 27 adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot undergoing electrophysiology study, CT-derived anatomic isthmus 3 width was significantly narrower in patients with slow-conducting isthmus 3 (18.4 ± 6.6 mm vs 29.2 ± 9.0 mm; p = 0.001), and width above 21.5 mm had an 80.0% negative predictive value. The authors propose CT isthmus measurement before pulmonary valve replacement as a non-invasive aid to invasive risk stratification.

papers.title: Twenty Years at the Crossroads: Is Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Science, Procedure, or Both?
papers.summary: A review/perspective reflecting on twenty years of clinical cardiac electrophysiology, examining whether the field is best characterized as science, procedure, or both, with attention to ablation, arrhythmology, atrial fibrillation, and training.

papers.title: Elucidating the relationship between protein amide I, II, and III bands and secondary structures by localized anharmonic vibrational calculations.
papers.summary: Used localized second-order vibrational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory combined with QM/MM and MD snapshot averaging to compute amide I, II, and III spectra of the insulin dimer and ubiquitin; found amide II and III peak positions closely track coil contributions, whereas the amide I maximum origin is more protein dependent, and hydrogen-bond-dependent amide I shifts correlate with O=C-N-H dihedral changes.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
